title: PlugMem — paper view
subtitle: The mechanism as Yang et al. describe it: three graphs G_E/G_S/G_P, Structuring → Retrieval → Reasoning. Lane = canonical stage; empty lanes (A6, B5) mean the paper defines no such step.
source: Yang et al. 2026, PlugMem (arXiv:2603.03296v1, ICML 2026)   ·   every anchor re-located in the paper text during verification (83 paper-side assertions: 65 ✓ / 1 ✗ / 17 ◐)
legend_notes: The headline: the paper writes multi-hop retrieval (stop-check ↔ query reformulation, B8↔B1) as the Retrieval Module's default behaviour, iterating to a hop cap — not an optional add-on. Compare the code view, where B8 is empty.
A6 INTERNALIZE and B5 SELECT are both empty by design: PlugMem never trains parameters, and RerankPrune's top-K cut is the only selection rule — no combinatorial optimizer.

The paper is internally inconsistent about whether one query can hit more than one memory type: Table 14 allows F⊆{E,S,P} but Listing 8's own prompt instructs the router to pick 'only one' (see mode_select).
Return scoring (ρ∈[1,10], an independent LLM judge) is a real, explicitly-described mechanism here — and the single biggest paper-only gap once you compare against code (see diff graph D2).
